query: What recurring types of problems show up in these incident tickets?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query by grouping tickets into recurring problem types. Values (vpn, network, database, email) are sound readings of the short_description text. Some overlap with the original 'category' column but the added values appear more granular/reliable, giving genuine grouping leverage.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Provides an orthogonal axis (how it failed: connection_failure, outage, access_denied) that is very useful for characterising recurring problems. Extractions match text well (e.g. 'Cannot connect' -> connection_failure). Some inference like 'not working properly' -> outage is a defensible but slightly strong reading; overall well grounded.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Gives a useful component-level grouping axis. Most values are warranted (WiFi -> network_infrastructure, VPN -> remote_access). However some are strong inferences: 'Cannot connect to database' -> server_side and 'Email system' -> client_application are guesses not explicitly stated in the terse text, so groundedness is only moderate.

per_column.name: scope_context
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs department vs production) is a reasonable analytical dimension. Where the text names a department it is well grounded; but 'individual_user' as the dominant value (313) is largely inferred by default when the text is silent, which risks asserting scope the source does not support.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Constant 'true' for all 500 rows. Near-constant column adds zero analytical leverage and cannot be grounded per-row since it distinguishes nothing; asserting recurrence uniformly is unsupported by the source text.

per_column.name: resolution_same_day
per_column.rationale: Derivable from opened_at/closed_at timestamps and correctly computed in samples. However it addresses resolution speed, not 'recurring types of problems', so its usefulness for THIS specific query is limited.

judge.rationale: The core columns (incident_category, failure_mode, affected_component, scope_context) form multiple genuine, well-grounded axes for identifying recurring problem types, directly serving the query. recurrence_signal is a dead constant that is both useless and unsupported, and resolution_same_day is well grounded but off-topic for this query. Some component/scope values rely on strong inference from terse descriptions, moderately lowering groundedness. No completeness penalty applied.
